extracted.addition: A briefing must never grant a dispatch authority to clear a control that exists to check that dispatch's own class of work; and running a review is not authorization to act on its outcome
extracted.sourceCitation: docs/state.md, 2026-08-08 checkpoint history, section "REVERTED: an agent moved a tripwire that exists to constrain agents" (~line 5895-5939: "a briefing must never hand a dispatch the authority to clear a control whose purpose is to check that dispatch's own class of work") and its own later self-correction in "NOT DONE: I stood the pin re-baseline down, because I had over-read the PO's authorization" (~line 6468-6508: "The PO authorized the review that was meant to inform the decision; they never said what to do with its result... Getting the separation of duties right does not supply the consent")
extracted.rationale: genuinely new durable rule, not covered by QG-04 (which is scoped literally to 'tests') or by any existing EL-03 approval-scope bullet in the exact form of clearing a tripwire; two live incidents in the same session (a reverted dispatch, then the orchestrator itself over-reading consent even after getting the separation-of-duties part right) make this a well-evidenced standing rule rather than a one-off narrative event. Given a new rule ID rather than folded into QG-04 because it applies beyond literal test files (pins, baselines, tamper-detection digests) and because it has a second, distinct clause (review-authorization != action-authorization) that QG-04 has no room for.

extracted.addition: (1) Model must be set via the dispatch tool's own model parameter, not only stated in the briefing text; (2) every path/commit-SHA/cross-reference cited in a briefing must be resolved against the actual repository before dispatching, not asserted from inference or memory
extracted.sourceCitation: docs/state.md, 2026-08-08 checkpoint history: bullet (1) from "PX0-AC-05 Critic dispatched — first round FAILed on my own dispatch error, not the code" (~line 4750-4778: model named in dispatch text as claude-opus-5/max but the Agent tool's own model parameter was never set, so the subagent silently ran as claude-sonnet-5; caught by the Critic's own report-header self-check). Bullet (2) is a recurring pattern named explicitly at least 4 times across this range as the same root cause (nonexistent sibling suite path ~line 6791-6798; wrong ADR filename ~line 6705-6712 including the self-quote "It is a checklist item or it is nothing"; wrong spec-section citation ~line 5383-5386; a search concluding 'implemented nowhere' from the wrong three directories ~line 6041-6046, self-named there as "A rule that only fires when you are suspicious is not a rule")
extracted.rationale: both are genuine sharpenings of EL-05's existing dispatch-metadata and briefing-duty language that the existing text does not yet state explicitly enough to have prevented these incidents: EL-05 already says 'the explicit model + effort for this dispatch' but does not say this must be a tool-call parameter, not prose; and EL-05/EL-09 do not yet carry an explicit reference-resolution duty distinct from the existing 'Verified claim hygiene' bullet, which governs claiming something IS verified rather than resolving a reference before citing it at all. Added as addenda to EL-05 rather than new rule IDs since both are refinements of the same briefing-duty rule EL-05 already governs, matching this repo's established extraction convention (see PHX-WP-STATE-EXTRACT-CHUNK-1's own record) of preferring cited addenda over minting a new ID for a close variant of an existing rule.
